headline.headline: MESSICK MASTERPIECE: RAYS BLANK GUARDIANS 1-0 ON A LONE FIFTH-INNING RUN
headline.deck: Tampa Bay pitcher dominates Cleveland in a crisp, 1:58 gem at Tropicana Field.
headline.body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — Parker Messick turned Sunday afternoon into an exercise in controlled dominance, shutting out the Cleveland Guardians across nine innings as the Tampa Bay Rays claimed a 1-0 victory before 20,562 fans at Tropicana Field. The only run of the afternoon came in the bottom of the fifth inning, when the Rays pushed across the game's lone tally against Cleveland starter Mason Rasmussen, who was otherwise sharp enough to keep Tampa Bay scoreless in every other frame.

Rasmussen's afternoon was not without incident. He hit Rays batter Halpin with a pitch, a moment that only added to the tension of what became one of the tightest, quickest games of the 2026 season. The contest was completed in 1 hour and 58 minutes, a testament to both pitching staffs' efficiency. For Cleveland, the loss stings in a division race where every game matters, as the Guardians were held to zero runs in all nine innings, never threatening to break through against Messick.

Messick earned the win, cementing himself as one of the more quietly effective starters in the American League this summer. The Rays, who have consistently punched above their payroll expectations, continue to manufacture wins through pitching and situational offense. Cleveland will look to regroup as the calendar turns toward August and the AL Central race tightens.

secondary.headline: NATIONALS ERUPT FOR 10 RUNS, SEND DIAMONDBACKS PACKING 10-7
secondary.deck: Washington's big fifth and seventh innings sink Arizona at Nationals Park.
secondary.body:
WASHINGTON — The Washington Nationals poured on four runs in the fifth inning and three more in the seventh to pull away from the Arizona Diamondbacks, 10-7, on Sunday at Nationals Park. Reliever Josefry Cornelio earned the win as Washington overcame an Arizona lead that the Diamondbacks built early, plating single runs in the first, third, and fourth innings to hold a 3-1 edge through four.

The Nationals answered emphatically in the fifth, blowing the game open with a four-run frame that flipped the momentum for good. Miles Mikolas hit Washington's Locklear with a pitch during the contest, adding friction to an afternoon that grew increasingly difficult for Arizona. A pinch-hit double by a Washington batter in the eighth inning kept the cushion comfortable despite a two-run Arizona rally in the ninth. Attendance was 21,341.

secondary.headline: BRAVES OUTLAST ORIOLES IN 11, TAKE ROAD WIN AT CAMDEN YARDS
secondary.deck: Atlanta's eleventh-inning run proves decisive in a grinding 3:31 marathon in Baltimore.
secondary.body:
BALTIMORE — The Atlanta Braves pushed across the decisive run in the top of the eleventh inning Sunday and held on to beat the Baltimore Orioles, 3-2, at Camden Yards in a grinding, 3-hour-31-minute contest attended by 25,032. Atlanta led 2-0 through seven innings before Baltimore rallied with single runs in the eighth and ninth to force extra innings, setting the stage for a tense conclusion.

Relievers R. Lopez, D. Young, and Nunez combined to earn the win for Atlanta, working through Baltimore's late-game threat and keeping the Orioles off the board in the eleventh after the Braves plated the go-ahead run. A walk issued to pinch hitter E. White in the eleventh helped set up Atlanta's winning rally. The Orioles, sitting at 51-55 and fourth in the AL East, have now dropped a winnable extra-innings game at home as their playoff hopes grow increasingly tenuous.

secondary.headline: NUGGETS MATCH OFFER SHEET, KEEP SPENCER JONES FROM THUNDER
secondary.deck: Denver retains young guard by matching Oklahoma City's two-year, $12 million bid.
secondary.body:
DENVER — The Denver Nuggets made their intentions clear Sunday, matching the Oklahoma City Thunder's fully guaranteed two-year, $12 million offer sheet for Spencer Jones and keeping the young guard in the Mile High City. The move signals Denver's commitment to retaining its depth pieces even as the franchise navigates the middle of the 2026 NBA playoff run, with the conference semifinals still ongoing.

Oklahoma City had submitted the offer sheet in an aggressive push to add perimeter depth, but the Nuggets exercised their right to match within the designated window. Jones, who has carved out a role in Denver's rotation, will now remain with the only NBA organization he has known at the professional level. The Thunder, themselves still competing in the postseason, will need to look elsewhere to address their backcourt needs before the roster-building window closes.

column.headline: MESSICK'S 1:58 GEM IS THE KIND OF BASEBALL THAT USED TO FILL STADIUMS
column.body:
Twenty thousand five hundred sixty-two people sat inside Tropicana Field on Sunday and watched something increasingly rare in the modern game: a complete, dominant pitching performance that was over before the afternoon got old. One hour and fifty-eight minutes. Nine innings. Zero runs allowed. Parker Messick did not need a bullpen, did not need a defensive shift adjustment in the seventh, and did not need a two-hour commercial break to finish the job. The Rays won 1-0, and the only question worth asking is why more fans were not there to see it.

The pitch-clock era was supposed to bring games like this back into fashion, and Sunday was proof the concept works. But 20,562 fans in a building that holds far more is a quiet indictment of how the Rays continue to be one of baseball's best-kept secrets. Messick deserved a full house. He got a half-empty one. The baseball was perfect. The crowd was not. Someone in Tampa Bay needs to fix that before another gem gets thrown into the void.

story.headline: METS BATTER DODGERS, 8-3, AS SEMIEN AND TAYLOR GOES DEEP AT CITI FIELD
story.deck: New York erupts for seven runs in sixth and seventh innings to send Los Angeles to defeat.
story.body:
NEW YORK — The New York Mets turned a 3-1 deficit into a rout Sunday afternoon, hammering the Los Angeles Dodgers 8-3 before 34,566 fans at Citi Field. The Mets scored three runs in the sixth inning and four more in the seventh to blow the game open, sending the defending champions to a lopsided defeat.

Marcus Semien launched his 11th home run of the season and Tyrone Taylor added his 8th as New York's offense broke through against a Dodgers pitching staff that had held the Mets scoreless through much of the middle innings. Los Angeles had taken a 3-1 lead through four frames, with two runs crossing in the third and one more in the fourth, but the Mets answered emphatically. Shohei Ohtani and Freddie Freeman each contributed doubles for the visitors, who stranded 22 runners on base and could not sustain any late threat.

Elsewhere in the National League, James Wood slugged his 30th home run and CJ Abrams connected for his 27th as Washington topped Arizona 10-7 in a slugfest at Nationals Park. The Nationals scored four times in the fifth and three more in the seventh to overcome an Arizona club that left a staggering 20 runners on base. In Pittsburgh, the Pirates survived a late Cubs rally to win 8-7, holding on after building an 8-1 lead through five innings before Chicago scored five times in the final two frames.

story.headline: LEBRON, KCP HEADED TO PHILLY AS SIXERS RELOAD FOR TITLE RUN
story.deck: James and Caldwell-Pope unite in Philadelphia while Denver locks up Spencer Jones.
story.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers are making noise this offseason, and the echoes are being felt across the entire NBA. LeBron James is officially a Sixer, and now Kentavious Caldwell-Pope is set to follow, agreeing to a buyout with the Memphis Grizzlies before planning to sign a one-year deal with Philadelphia. Rich Paul, James' longtime agent, revealed Sunday that the road to LeBron's decision was an emotional roller coaster that did not resolve cleanly, making the eventual commitment to Philly all the more significant. The 76ers, still searching for their first championship since 1983, have now surrounded their core with two of the more decorated veterans available this summer.

Caldwell-Pope, a two-time champion with the Los Angeles Lakers and Denver Nuggets, brings the kind of defensive tenacity and championship pedigree that Sixers president Daryl Morey has long coveted. The 33-year-old shooting guard averaged double figures in Memphis last season and shot better than 38 percent from three-point range. His arrival gives Philadelphia a versatile perimeter defender who has guarded the opposition's best wing in the biggest moments, a role he can fill immediately alongside James and a retooled supporting cast.

Meanwhile, in Denver, the Nuggets moved swiftly to protect their depth by matching the Oklahoma City Thunder's fully guaranteed two-year, $12 million offer sheet for restricted free agent Spencer Jones. The Thunder had aggressively pursued the 24-year-old wing, who shot 42 percent from beyond the arc in limited minutes last season off Denver's bench. The Nuggets exercised their matching rights before the deadline, ensuring Jones remains part of the rotation that won the 2023 NBA title. In Cleveland, the Cavaliers added veteran forward Mario Hezonja on a one-year, $2.8 million deal, reuniting the former No. 5 overall pick from the 2015 draft with a contender hungry for frontcourt depth heading into October.

story.headline: GRANATO STEPS BACK AS CANUCKS SHUFFLE FRONT OFFICE AMID BUSY OFFSEASON
story.deck: Hockey Hall of Famer moves to adviser role while Blue Jackets lock up Sillinger and Greaves
story.body:
Hockey Hall of Fame forward Cammi Granato is transitioning out of her assistant general manager role with the Vancouver Canucks and into an adviser position, the team announced Monday, reshaping a front office that has been active throughout the summer. Granato, who made history when she was named one of the first female assistant GMs in NHL history, will remain with the organization in a reduced capacity as the Canucks continue to build toward a playoff contender in the Western Conference.

In Columbus, the Blue Jackets moved swiftly to shore up their roster on two fronts, avoiding an arbitration hearing with forward Cole Sillinger by agreeing to a three-year contract worth $13.875 million. The 21-year-old center, a former first-round pick, posted back-to-back productive seasons for a Columbus squad that is trending upward under general manager Don Waddell. Hours later, the Blue Jackets also locked up goaltender Jet Greaves on a three-year, $15 million deal running through the 2028-29 season, betting heavily on the young netminder as their franchise cornerstone between the pipes.

Meanwhile, veteran coach John Tortorella confirmed he was left stinging by the Vegas Golden Knights' decision not to retain him following a surprising postseason run, telling reporters he was quote disappointed unquote by the move. Tortorella, one of the most decorated bench bosses in the modern NHL with 900-plus career wins, said he remains eager to return to coaching and expects opportunities to surface as teams assess their situations heading into the fall.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS NFL TEAMS RESHAPE ROSTERS FOR 2026
story.deck: Three veteran signal-callers change addresses as franchises bet big on new faces.
story.body:
The NFL offseason turned into a full-blown quarterback market this spring, with veteran passers landing in unexpected places across the league. Kirk Cousins, released by the Atlanta Falcons after a disappointing two-year run, agreed to a one-year prove-it deal with the Las Vegas Raiders, giving the perennial rebuilding franchise a steady hand under center while rookie prospects develop on the depth chart. Meanwhile, the Carolina Panthers moved aggressively to acquire a proven starter rather than endure another developmental season, sending a package of draft picks to the New England Patriots in exchange for journeyman starter Jacoby Brissett.

The 2026 NFL Draft delivered its share of surprises when the Tennessee Titans used the fourth overall pick on Colorado wide receiver Travis Hunter Jr., a name that had climbed draft boards throughout the winter scouting process. The Jacksonville Jaguars, desperate to surround Trevor Lawrence with weapons after his injury-riddled 2025 campaign, doubled down at receiver in the second round, nabbing two pass-catchers before addressing their battered offensive line in day three. Draft analysts from NFL Network called Jacksonville's haul among the most targeted and disciplined approaches of any club over the three-day event in Green Bay.

Training camps remain two months away, but roster battles are already taking shape through organized team activities. The San Francisco 49ers, coming off a second-round playoff exit in the 2025 season, are watching rookie linebacker Darius Colton turn heads during OTA sessions in Santa Clara, with defensive coordinator Nick Sorensen praising the rookie's instincts against the run. The Dallas Cowboys, meanwhile, quietly re-signed aging pass rusher Micah Parsons to a restructured contract, betting that the 27-year-old can return to Pro Bowl form after knee surgery kept him limited through much of last season.
